messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran an apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic comparison and saw ~15% p50 latency regression when the client harness disables HTTP keepalive.
maya: ouch. is that with the same kernel selection and batching heuristics?
alex: yes, kernel=auto, batching=dynamic(32ms,min_batch=1), kv_cache=on (warm). quant=4bit. only variable was keepalive=false in the replay harness.
samir: 15% sounds like connection churn + TLS handshake + Nagle interplay. do you have conn counts?
alex: short paste from the harness metrics: 
```
requests: 20000
connections_opened: 19870
avg_requests_per_connection: 1.0065
tls_handshakes/sec: 180
cpu_user: +12% vs baseline
```
joanne: that avg_requests_per_connection is a red flag — basically one request per TCP socket. that's not apples-to-apples vs a real client.
maya: exact. synthetic clients historically default to short-lived sockets unless you tweak keepalive and pool size. we should compare: 1) replay with keepalive=true and pool=50, 2) synthetic with prewarmed sockets, 3) replay with connection priming enabled.
ben: Also remember Nagle interacts with small writes — gRPC tends to avoid coalescing; HTTP/1.1 with small chunked frames + Nagle can add 1-2 RTTs unless TCP_NODELAY set. Did the harness toggle TCP_NODELAY?
alex: we didn't. default harness uses kernel defaults. changed to tcp_nodelay=true and re-ran quick smoke: p50 recovered ~7% but still ~8% above baseline.
samir: residual 8% could be TLS late handshake (session resumption not used) or kernel scheduling for short-lived sockets. Try session resumption + keepalive.
alex: enabled session resumption (session tickets) & keepalive on client, p50 now within 1.5% of baseline. so main vector was handshake + conn churn.
joanne: good catch. this means our earlier regression ticket (perf/regress/421) might be a false positive if tests had keepalive off. we should tag the harness config in the CI artifact.
maya: Agreed. Proposal: add an apples-to-apples checklist to the client harness README: kernel selection, keepalive, pool size, tcp_nodelay, tls_session_resumption, kv_cache_warm. Minimal config snippet: 
```
client:
  keepalive: true
  pool_size: 50
  tcp_nodelay: true
  tls:
    session_resumption: true
server:
  kernel: auto
  batching:
    mode: dynamic
    max_delay_ms: 32
  kv_cache: warm
```
ben: Also add a small script to prime sockets and KV cache before measurement (10s warmup with production-ish payloads). saves a ton of flakiness.
ci-bot: build/bench/2141592000 completed — artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/2141592000/ (configs, pcap, flamegraphs)
alex: uploaded a pcap and per-socket timeline to that artifact. next steps: 1) run full regression with checklist applied, 2) re-open perf/regress/421 if still failing, 3) update docs + harness defaults.
samir: also add an invariant check in the harness that flags avg_requests_per_connection < 3 as a warning for long-tail test modes.
maya: I'll make a PR with the checklist + default change to keepalive=true and a priming job. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :eyes:
alex: thanks — saved us chasing kernel/batching heuristics when it was client-side churn.
joanne: note to self: include KV cache eviction radar in next run — even warm caches degrade with too many short connections.
alex: noted. scheduling follow-ups in the bench board. :white_check_mark:
